_comment: Scripts that ARE bulk content operations and are owed a playbook, but do not have one yet.
This is deliberately NOT non-bulk-allowlist.json. That file means 'this is not a bulk
operation'. Putting content:generate there would assert something false, and the next
person reading it would believe it. These entries assert the opposite: each one is a real
bulk op, and its absence from the registry is debt.
The distinction matters because registering a playbook is not a lint fix. A registry entry
carries a params_schema, a kill switch, a quota-ledger binding, and an estimator whose cost
and duration are shown to an operator before they authorise spend. An invented estimate is
worse than no playbook, so these are recorded rather than fabricated.
The list may shrink freely as each script gets a real playbook. Growing it takes a reviewed
edit, which is where someone asks whether the new bulk script should have been a playbook
from the start. Same ratchet as fork-test-lint-baseline.json and gif-scene-baseline.json.

owed.reason: Scrapes GATE, OpenStax and OCW corpora in one run. Needs a per-source quota and a kill switch; cost is bandwidth and time, not tokens.
Builds explainers across the whole concept set. Estimator needs a per-explainer token cost that nobody has measured yet.
The main content generation job. Spend is real and per-run; this is the one that most needs a dry-run estimate before it becomes a playbook.
Shell wrapper around content:generate that loops unattended. Should not exist as a bare script at all once the playbook has a kill switch.
Generates stance variants across a topic. Bounded work, but still bulk LLM spend with no ledger binding today.
Batch Wolfram verification. Rate-limited and metered per request; verify-sweep is the registered playbook that supersedes it, so this may be deleted rather than registered.
